Stumps on day 4 = 18:03 local, 16:03 GMT, 21:33 IST: Phewf! How do you describe that? Test cricket never fails to amaze us. Just when you think, there's no life left, you would often see resurrection through a fiery spell or a stubborn knock. And when two batters combine to breathe new life and bring back balance into the contest, it's gotta be extra special. Been that kinda day for Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder who both played the finest innings of their international career thus far. The day started off with a lead of 40 with 6 wickets in the bank and an all-out inside two sessions looked inevitable. Not to be. While Rickelton engineered a 50-run stand with Breetzke, he then joined hands with Mulder to notch up the most valuable partnership of this series. The pair added 154 for the 6th wicket and the most impressive bit about their assocation was that they barely gave any sniff to their opposition.

South Africa’s 387 is their third-highest total against Australia at Cape Town, behind 651 in 2009 (2nd innings) and 473 in 2002 (3rd innings).

A successful 288-run chase would be the second-highest at Cape Town, behind Australia's own 331 in 2002.

Brian McMillan (103*) & L Klusener (102*) vs IND, Cape Town, 1997
Faf du Plessis (137) & Dean Elgar (103*) vs NZ, Gqeberha, 2013
Ryan Rickelton (101) & Wiaan Mulder (115) vs AUS, Cape Town, 2026*

So solid was the duo, it needed a brilliant fielding effort from Inglis to pull curtains on their partnership. Once Rickelton fell, the hosts lost their next 3 wickets for 16 runs. Mulder was on 82 when number 11, Rabada, walked out to bat. The all-rounder then took things into his control and only exposed Rabada for a maximum of 2 balls per over. Eventually, he claimed his 4th Test ton and never lost patience despite the drought of boundaries. Skill. Character. Grit - You name it, and the home team had every answer to the Aussies. They did it all with no fuss. That said, Australia tried hard but their bowling wasn't as incisive and consistent as it was yesterday. And therefore, find themselves chasing 288 on a surface that seem to have a few tricks for the spinners. Can Harmer and Co. back it up tomorrow? Travis Head to belt a hundred before lunch? What predictions have you got? Join us early tomorrow for what promises to be a fitting final day of the series. Cheers!!

12:33 Local Time, 10:33 GMT, 16:03 IST: Ironic that a match which saw so many fightbacks at different stages is now ending with a whimper. Australia have been ripped apart on the final day here in Cape Town, losing seven wickets in the opening session. Rabada started the procession with two in the first over, removing Renshaw and Labuschagne. He then got rid of Head as well before Harmer took over and laid out an absolute masterclass of off-spin bowling. The scorecard cuts a sorry figure for the visitors with as many as six batters being dismissed for single digits. There was such excitement at the start of the day about all the posibilities of a close contest. It's all coming to an anti-climactic end, not that South Africa are complaining. We'll be back to wrap it all up after the break.
